content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an AI agent pane; read `AGENTS.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` first. Sending a print goes through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog (SelectMachineDialog for Bambu printers), reskinned in JusPrin colours and otherwise unchanged by decision (product definition section 2.9: JusPrin builds no checklist in front of it, the agent may open it but never presses Send, and learns whether a job went out from the printer's state afterwards). A print-history design exists on the "JusPrin v2" design canvas (page "Print history": one record per G-code, the chat keeps one-line markers) but is not implemented; `ProjectPersistence` has a ledger of physical prints with `subscribe_ledger`. On 2026-10-28 a UX walkthrough of the built app (jusprin-newui a684aee37d, Opus 5.5) rated this high; critique with screenshots at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (frames 1A-08 to 1A-12). Kenneth wants to choose between fix options before code is written: first deliverable is an untracked options note in the worktree root, then stop. Rules: fork-stewardship doc before touching OrcaSlicer-owned files; use `Slic3r::GUI::MessageDialog` never wxMessageBox; temp docs untracked; do not commit unless asked. Reproduce with the in-process fake Bambu printer (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`): scratch copy of the .app and of `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2`, `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}`, `presets.machine` "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", `local_machines` set to `{}` (an empty-id entry makes the fake agent loop), launch with `--datadir <scratch>`, open `~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf`, slice, Print, map the "?" slot to A1, Send, Confirm. The fake never changes to "printing" by itself; write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` with `{"state":"printing","progress":0.1}` to simulate the printer starting.

Task:
Problem: after the person presses Send in the send dialog and Confirm on its "unknown filaments" warning, the dialog closes and nothing else changes: no line in the chat, no change on the printer chip or header, and the "1 print issue" chip stays. The app log shows `print_job: send ok` and the fake printer's `start_local_print`, so the job did go out. The person cannot tell. Frame 1A-12 of the critique shows the screen after Send; 1A-08 to 1A-11 show the dialog chain before it.

Task, in this order:
1. Reproduce it in the real app (recipe in the background notes). Find where the send result is known to the app: the send dialog's job completion in OrcaSlicer's code (search `print_job: send ok` and `on_send_print`), and what the fork already subscribes to (the print ledger in `ProjectPersistence`, the printer chip's state source, the chat's one-line markers in the page's `MessageList`). Check whether the ledger already records this send and simply has no reader.
2. Write an untracked options note (`sent-print-ack-options.md` in the worktree root) with two to four options, each with what the person sees and when, the OrcaSlicer-owned lines touched and their rebase cost, and a recommendation. Candidates: a quiet one-line chat marker "Sent to Bambu Lab A1 mini · 10:42" the moment the dialog reports success, drawn like the "Opened … as a new project" line; a transient confirmation above the issue chip, which already exists for export and arrange outcomes (see "Print issues and OrcaSlicer's notifications" in `agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md`); the printer chip showing "Sending…" then the printer's state; an app-started agent turn after the send, which the product definition argues against. Say how each relates to the unimplemented print-history design so the chosen one is not thrown away later.
3. Stop and wait for Kenneth to choose. Do not implement before he answers.

Done, after his choice, means: within a second of a successful send the person sees a confirmation naming the printer, and a failed send is visible as such; verified in the real app with the fake printer and a screenshot; any OrcaSlicer-owned change recorded as fork-stewardship requires.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. # Handoff: G-code and print history

Written 2026-10-27, rewritten the same evening after Kenneth and I redesigned it. Temporary working doc: keep it untracked, never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.

## In short

JusPrin keeps **one record per G-code** that left a project: where it went (exported files, sends to printers) and what the printer reported about each print of it (printing, finished). Slicing by itself writes nothing. **No failure state anywhere** (decided 2026-10-27): there is no reliable way to know a print failed, so nothing records, badges or discusses a failure.

That record is shown on **one full-view screen, "Print history"**, reached from Home and from the project. The chat only gets a one-line marker when a G-code leaves the project. The old design, where the chat held G-code entries and a dark failed-print band, is retired: its boards are deleted or redrawn. A print that went wrong is something the person tells the agent in chat; the history gives the G-code and its settings for that conversation.

The app is far behind: it persists `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` but never writes them outside tests, has no export record, and the model never sees print history. The next job is to implement the drawn design.

## Where the design lives

- **Current canvas, the source of truth:** https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ ("JusPrin v2"), version 1793148719-e71c or later (checked against the published file list on 2026-10-27: history-01…05 present, history-06 and agent-ui-01 gone, comp-plates-pane, main-05/07/09 and plates-26e3 updated). New page **"Print history"** (id `print-history`):
  - `history-01-all-prints`: the screen with no filter.
  - `history-02-project-garage-bracket`: filtered to one project.
  - `history-03-printer-bambu-x1c`: filtered to one printer.
  - `history-04-entry-states`: every row state of an entry, and the no-failure-state rule. This replaces the deleted `agent-ui-01` chat-timeline state matrix.
  - `history-05-ways-in`: the Home header link, project cards, printer cards and the project pane row that open the screen.
  - (`history-06-discuss-in-current-chat` was drawn and deleted the same day when failure states were dropped.)
  - Main Page: `main-05`, `main-07`, `main-09` now show one-line G-code markers in the chat instead of entries and a band.
  - Plates & Project Pane: `plates-26e3` ("Project · print history row") and `plates-26e4` ("Project · never printed"; the file is still named `count-only-print-history`). Both import `comp-plates-pane`, whose Project tab was redrawn.
- **Frozen, history only:** the previous canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, the old Claude Design project "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts", and Figma (retired 2026-10-20). They show the chat-entry design and how it was reached, never the current design.
- Memory note for agents: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/print-history-screen-design.md`.

## The design (decided 2026-10-27)

### The record

Every print has three keys: the project it came from, the G-code it ran, and the printer it ran on. That is one table. The project view and the printer view are filters over it, so they can never disagree.

The **G-code record** (decided 2026-10-27 in a forked session, relayed here by that session; Kenneth's words were "go with your recommendations"):

- **Identity:** a hash of the G-code file bytes, computed at export or send time, before the file leaves. The existing `manufacturing_input_hash` stays beside it as the link to the checkpoint. Displayed as eight hex digits in two groups ("a71f 8c04").
- **Shape:** one record per G-code holding its lists of destinations (exports, sends) and prints. Export and send create the record or append to it. The separate `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` events are replaced, not kept beside it.
- **Bytes:** JusPrin keeps a copy of every sent or exported G-code in the project's aux directory next to the checkpoints, capped at the last N G-codes per project (N chosen in code). Older entries show a "file no longer kept, re-slice" state instead of Print again.

An **entry** is one G-code:

- Header: name (the exported file name, else the plate name), short hash in monospace as a secondary id, the stats line ("2h 34m · 69 g · 181 layers"), the time. The project name shows only when no project filter is on.
- "Made with Bambu X1C · Gray PETG · 0.20 Strong · Open in chat". Open in chat jumps to the marker in the chat where this G-code went out.
- One row per **destination**:
  - Export: `matches, checked just now` (green check); `changed outside JusPrin` (greyed, warning glyph, Export again); `not found` (greyed, Export again). Greyed means opacity, never strike-through. Export again writes a new file beside a changed one, it does not overwrite.
  - Send: `sending…`; `sent, delivery not confirmed`; `on the printer's SD · started` or `· not started`. A send never gets a check mark: only a hashed file is verified. Use the printer's own name, not its model.
- One row per **print**, only what the printer reports: Printing (the only live fact drawn; progress stays on the printer card) and Finished. **No Failed, Didn't go well or Cancelled row.** Kenneth, 2026-10-27: "I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed." Cancelled goes with them because a Bambu reports a person's stop as a failed state and the two cannot be told apart. A print that stopped early simply never gets a Finished row.
- Actions: **Print again** and **Export…**. Reprint lives only here. Kenneth: the common question is "which version am I printing", so a reprint must be attached to a specific G-code, never to a project or a printer.

### The screen

- Full view in place of the plater, like Home. Top bar: back arrow, "Print history", preferences gear. No printer chip, no plate button.
- Home and Project are the roots; Print history is always a leaf. Back returns to where it was opened from. Nothing opens on top of it: Open in chat and the printer link go to a root.
- Filters are removable chips ("Project: Garage bracket ×", "Printer: Bambu X1C ×"). Where you came from sets the first chip; remove it and the list widens to everything. Entries are grouped by day, newest first. A search box filters by text.

### Ways in

- Home header: a "Print history" link, unfiltered.
- Each Home project card: a history line ("2 prints · 1 printing now", "1 print · finished Sun") that opens the screen filtered to the project. No failure badge.
- Each Home printer card: a history line ("12 prints · 1 printing now") filtered to the printer.
- Project pane, Project tab: the Print history view is now one row (count, latest outcome) with a chevron into the screen. A project that never printed says "Nothing printed or exported yet".

### The chat

- When a G-code leaves the project, one marker line between turns: "▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history". Nothing else.
- Nothing about a print going wrong is recorded or drawn anywhere. The person tells the agent in chat ("it shifted off the plate"); the agent reads the recent G-codes and their settings from the history in its state and reasons from there. There is no Discuss link, no attachment and no recording tool.

### What is deliberately not drawn

- No Stale badge, no live progress card, no completed-print card in the chat, no entry with zero destinations, no failure state of any kind. Slicing writes nothing.

## Decision history

| When | What happened |
|---|---|
| Aug 7 – Sep 1 | Old Design project: setup card, "Prints" chip, "the chat is the timeline". Phase 6 (51a97b1bdf, 2026-09-01) adds BuildRecord, ExportedCopyRecord, PhysicalPrintRecord with chat cards. |
| Sep 10 | Kenneth: slicing writes nothing; entries only for G-code that left the project; no Stale. |
| Sep 11 | "Revert here" removed (dcb06059f3). |
| Oct 2–3 | Print history moves to the Project tab in the left pane (`Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp`). |
| Oct 26 | dbec3e3a38 removes BuildRecord and ExportedCopyRecord, adds `SentRecord`. 71c1791e39 (docs only) specifies that sending goes through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog and that an agent tool `print_dialog_open` may open it; the tool was never implemented. |

- **Fork stewardship** (`agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`): export, send and printer status live in OrcaSlicer-owned files. Bind the existing events (`EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED`, `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, the print-host progress) from fork code rather than editing the handlers; one seam each. The PR must carry the rebase simulation (`git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD`) with both endpoint commits, an account of every upstream line changed, and a statement of what the fork now owns.

- **Wording**: a file is exported, sent, opened or loaded, never "arrived" (`AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the model-facing text).
- **Errors**: no catch-and-log; invalid transitions (a print without its G-code, a hash mismatch on a kept copy) fail visibly.

## The design (decided 2026-10-27)

### The record

Every print has three keys: the project it came from, the G-code it ran, and the printer it ran on. That is one table. The project view and the printer view are filters over it, so they can never disagree.

The **G-code record** (decided 2026-10-27 in a forked session, relayed here by that session; Kenneth's words were "go with your recommendations"):

- **Identity:** a hash of the G-code file bytes, computed at export or send time, before the file leaves. The existing `manufacturing_input_hash` stays beside it as the link to the checkpoint. Displayed as eight hex digits in two groups ("a71f 8c04").
- **Shape:** one record per G-code holding its lists of destinations (exports, sends) and prints. Export and send create the record or append to it. The separate `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` events are replaced, not kept beside it.
- **Bytes:** JusPrin keeps a copy of every sent or exported G-code in the project's aux directory next to the checkpoints, capped at the last N G-codes per project (N chosen in code). Older entries show a "file no longer kept, re-slice" state instead of Print again.

An **entry** is one G-code:

- Header: name (the exported file name, else the plate name), short hash in monospace as a secondary id, the stats line ("2h 34m · 69 g · 181 layers"), the time. The project name shows only when no project filter is on.
- "Made with Bambu X1C · Gray PETG · 0.20 Strong · Open in chat". Open in chat jumps to the marker in the chat where this G-code went out.
- One row per **destination**:
  - Export: `matches, checked just now` (green check); `changed outside JusPrin` (greyed, warning glyph, Export again); `not found` (greyed, Export again). Greyed means opacity, never strike-through. Export again writes a new file beside a changed one, it does not overwrite.
  - Send: `sending…`; `sent, delivery not confirmed`; `on the printer's SD · started` or `· not started`. A send never gets a check mark: only a hashed file is verified. Use the printer's own name, not its model.
- One row per **print**, only what the printer reports: Printing (the only live fact drawn; progress stays on the printer card) and Finished. **No Failed, Didn't go well or Cancelled row.** Kenneth, 2026-10-27: "I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed." Cancelled goes with them because a Bambu reports a person's stop as a failed state and the two cannot be told apart. A print that stopped early simply never gets a Finished row.
- Actions: **Print again** and **Export…**. Reprint lives only here. Kenneth: the common question is "which version am I printing", so a reprint must be attached to a specific G-code, never to a project or a printer.

### The screen

- Full view in place of the plater, like Home. Top bar: back arrow, "Print history", preferences gear. No printer chip, no plate button.
- Home and Project are the roots; Print history is always a leaf. Back returns to where it was opened from. Nothing opens on top of it: Open in chat and the printer link go to a root.
- Filters are removable chips ("Project: Garage bracket ×", "Printer: Bambu X1C ×"). Where you came from sets the first chip; remove it and the list widens to everything. Entries are grouped by day, newest first. A search box filters by text.

### Ways in

- Home header: a "Print history" link, unfiltered.
- Each Home project card: a history line ("2 prints · 1 printing now", "1 print · finished Sun") that opens the screen filtered to the project. No failure badge.
- Each Home printer card: a history line ("12 prints · 1 printing now") filtered to the printer.
- Project pane, Project tab: the Print history view is now one row (count, latest outcome) with a chevron into the screen. A project that never printed says "Nothing printed or exported yet".

### The chat

- When a G-code leaves the project, one marker line between turns: "▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history". Nothing else.
- Nothing about a print going wrong is recorded or drawn anywhere. The person tells the agent in chat ("it shifted off the plate"); the agent reads the recent G-codes and their settings from the history in its state and reasons from there. There is no Discuss link, no attachment and no recording tool.

### What is deliberately not drawn

- No Stale badge, no live progress card, no completed-print card in the chat, no entry with zero destinations, no failure state of any kind. Slicing writes nothing.

## Rules that apply to this work

- **Fork stewardship** (`agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`): export, send and printer status live in OrcaSlicer-owned files. Bind the existing events (`EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED`, `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, the print-host progress) from fork code rather than editing the handlers; one seam each. The PR must carry the rebase simulation (`git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD`) with both endpoint commits, an account of every upstream line changed, and a statement of what the fork now owns.
- **UI values** (`agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, "Writing UI code"): every colour, radius, font and control size comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, through `ShellTheme` and `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp` natively and through the CSS variables on the web pages. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first.
- **Wording**: a file is exported, sent, opened or loaded, never "arrived" (`AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the model-facing text).
- **Errors**: no catch-and-log; invalid transitions (a print without its G-code, a hash mismatch on a kept copy) fail visibly.
- **Working docs** stay untracked; commit code, tests and standing guides only.

## What the app needs (in rough order)

1. **A G-code record**: file-bytes hash (the id), name, plate, time, stats, printer, material, profile, `manufacturing_input_hash` (the checkpoint link), the chat and message it went out from, and its lists of destinations and prints. It replaces `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` in `ManufacturingHistory.hpp` and the `add_sent` / `add_physical_print` API in `ProjectStateDocument`. Nothing in the app ever wrote those, so there is nothing to preserve beyond a migration note: a 3MF that carries them (possible only from tests or the Phase 6 era) is read without error and the old events are dropped or, if cheap, folded into records keyed by their `manufacturing_input_hash`.
2. **Writers**: the export path (`EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED` after `on_process_completed`, and the `export_file` tool) and the send paths (`EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, print-host progress 100 with `post_action`) hash the file bytes before the file leaves, then create or append the record; printer status writes printing and finished only.
2a. **Kept copies**: on every send or export, copy the G-code into the project's aux directory beside the checkpoints; keep the last N per project and mark older records "file no longer kept, re-slice".
3. **File checks**: hash the exported file when the screen opens and on demand; three states (matches, changed, not found).
4. **The screen** as a second screen of the Home web page (`HomeUI`, which has no routing today), with the filter chips and the one-level back; host messages to open it with a filter and to go back; the ways in: Home header link, card lines, project pane row. Opening from the project selects `tpHome` and names the screen and filter.
5. **Print again** for a recorded G-code: open OrcaSlicer's send dialog for the kept copy (step 2a) instead of the current slice. The `print_dialog_open` tool is specified in the tool guide but not built; build it so both the screen and the agent use it. When the copy is gone, the entry offers re-slice instead.
6. **Chat**: the marker line replaces `ManufacturingHistoryCard`; Open in chat scrolls to it.
7. **Model context**: a manufacturing-history field on `AgentRequest`, filled in `make_agent_request` and emitted by `workspace_json`, so the agent knows what left the project, how each print ended, and can diff a failed G-code's settings (by `manufacturing_input_hash`) against the current setup. Not a new prompt section.

158:### Print issues and OrcaSlicer's notifications
159-
160-Inside the shell OrcaSlicer's own notifications are held but not drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds: print problems as a status pill in the canvas's lower right corner, the list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is about, with **Ask AI** and **Resolve with AI**; the outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused) as a short confirmation above the pill; and work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export) as an entry in the chat.
161-
162-**OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth.** A notification carries a kind, a level and words. It does not carry the object it is about, so where OrcaSlicer lets its check be asked again, that check is asked once more for the object only.
163-
164-| Piece | Owns |
165-|---|---|
166-| `PrintIssues/NoticeKinds` | Where each of OrcaSlicer's notification kinds goes: the issue list, a confirmation, running work, application state, or nowhere. Every kind is named; a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in this file until someone routes it. |
167-| `PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor` | Reads the list on the notification manager's own turn, compares it with what it saw last, and rebuilds only on a change. Asks OrcaSlicer's checks for the object behind a validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an object out of a nozzle's reach and a slicing step warning. Holds no rule about what a problem is. |
168-| `issues_from` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue` | The rule, as plain data with its own tests: an object lookup's entry exists only while OrcaSlicer holds a notification of its kind; a print-problem notification no lookup answers for is a plate-wide issue in OrcaSlicer's words. |
169-| `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout`, `IssueOverlay` | Where the pieces go, how they are drawn and how they close, with ImGui inside the canvas's frame through the same overlay hook as the tool strip. The bubble never covers its object, the pill, a confirmation or the tool strip. |
170-| `PrintIssues/WorkFeed` | Work as it starts, moves on and ends. A slice is followed through OrcaSlicer's own events, which carry a percentage and an outcome. Other work is read from the "still running" notifications, which carry neither. |
171-| `AgentHost::begin_work`, `update_work`, `finish_work`; `WorkCard` in the page | The entry in the chat: saved with the project at the place in the timeline where the work started, so a later message reads below it; a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel while it runs; completed in place. The chat panel opens when work starts. Repeats are folded by the page, never in what is saved, and an entry still "running" in a project that was closed mid-run reads as interrupted. |
172-| `PrintIssues/IssueContext`, `AgentHost::submit_issue_message` | The chat message a button sends, and the one way a message enters the chat from outside the page. |
173-
174-Two things are read whether or not a notification exists, because OrcaSlicer's notifications do not cover them in time:
175-
176-- **The slice result.** A path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach, and a filament that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when OrcaSlicer's preview loads the slice, which here means opening Check print. OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the moment the slice ends.
177-- **Why a slice failed.** A critical failure is shown in a dialog and leaves no notification, and no notification says which object the failure named. `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` is the only place both exist.
178-
179-Rules that follow:
180-
181-- **No pill is the all-clear, and it is never given before a check.** The pill is drawn only while OrcaSlicer reports an issue, ignored ones included. While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the last issues are kept, the pill says it is checking and both buttons are off, so the pill does not go until OrcaSlicer has looked. An issue that was not in the list before is announced once by a ring that spreads from the pill twice; an edit that keeps an issue, and ignoring one or undoing that, announce nothing.
182-- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
183-- **"Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's answer.** An error-level notification blocks. For the slice result it is OrcaSlicer's own post-slice check, which allows a path 2 mm past the plate edge; the monitor does not apply a stricter test of its own.
184-- **The object is never read out of the words.** Two messages of one kind are told apart by comparing OrcaSlicer's words now with its words before, as OrcaSlicer does itself. Which object a message is about always comes from a check's own ids.
185-- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **The two buttons differ only in the sentence**: Ask AI and Resolve with AI send the same context and the turn gets the same tools.
186-- **Operation failures are not print issues.** A failed download or a refused arrange is a confirmation, never an entry in the issue list.
187-- **Closing hides, it never resolves.** The pill is always there and is the way back; the list and the bubble are opened and closed, one at a time, and closing either changes nothing about the issue or the count. The list closes on a pick, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. Turning the view or dragging the object leaves it open. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on **Ask AI** or **Resolve with AI** that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the pill opens the bubble directly, and with several the bubble's pager walks them all. The overlay hears Escape and presses through handlers of its own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.
188-- **Ignoring a warning is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's.** **Ignore this warning** in the bubble leaves OrcaSlicer's notification alone: the warning stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the pill stops counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left, never "No print issues"). Only a warning can be ignored; a blocker cannot, because OrcaSlicer would still refuse to print. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that warning on the active plate's own list, and is forgotten when OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not saved with the project. The rule is `mark_ignored` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue`.

---
name: drive-app-with-posted-key-events
description: "Drive the built JusPrin app headlessly (even with the screen locked) by posting CGEvents to its pid with a tiny Swift tool; keys work, mouse clicks do not, and the send dialog is reachable by keyboard."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6b96dccc-1cb4-4f72-9de4-3ecee4b28e74
  modified: 2026-09-08T05:58:16.222Z
---

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].

## 2.9 Sending a print

This surface answers: **Is the correct job about to be sent to the correct physical machine?**

The answer is OrcaSlicer's own send dialog, kept as it is and shown in JusPrin's colours. JusPrin builds no checklist screen in front of it or in its place, so sending a print takes one dialog. Prepare has a visible Print entry point, and Print opens that dialog; nothing sends without it:

`Print -> OrcaSlicer's send dialog -> the person presses Send`

For a printer on Bambu's network the dialog is Select Machine (`SelectMachineDialog`). For a Klipper or OctoPrint printer it is OrcaSlicer's upload dialog (`Plater::send_gcode_legacy`). The person opens it with Print, or the agent opens it when the person asks to print.

### Why OrcaSlicer's dialog stays

- It already holds the choices made at send time: the destination printer, the plate, filament-to-slot mapping (including AMS), plate type, bed leveling, flow calibration, nozzle offset calibration, timelapse, and the Send button.
- It fills them in itself. It opens on the selected printer, works out the slot mapping, restores the options last used for that printer model, and refuses to send while it shows a problem such as a filament mismatch or a busy printer.
- It is large and changes often upstream: about 5,400 lines, and 93 upstream commits in the year to October 2026, crash fixes and new printers among them. Upstream is also moving other printer families onto it (`a5413efc37`, printer agents for Moonraker and Qidi). The unchanged dialog takes all of that at each rebase; a JusPrin replacement would have to keep pace with it.

The reskin goes through the brand palette (see [Design system](design-system.md)). A colour the dialog hard-codes, which the palette cannot reach, needs a seam that follows [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md), not a change to the dialog's layout.

The printer's own detection settings (first-layer inspection, build-plate detection, tangle and nozzle-clumping detection, AI failure detection and how readily it pauses) belong to the printer, not to one job. They live with Printer Configuration and Monitor, not in the send.

### Why the agent cannot decide this alone

This is where digital assumptions become a real physical operation. The chosen printer may be occupied, prepared with another plate, located remotely, or loaded with valuable material.

Some monitoring options also involve privacy, camera use, false-positive tolerance, or printer-specific limitations.

### What the agent should do

The agent gets the project ready before the send: the printer, a plate type that matches the plate on the bed, filaments that match what is loaded, and a valid slice of the plate. Those are what OrcaSlicer's dialog reads when it opens. When the person asks to print, the agent opens the dialog and says in one line anything in it worth a look, such as turning on flow calibration for a new filament. It does not change the dialog's options, and it never presses Send.

The dialog is modal. While it is open the person cannot type in the Agent pane, and the agent cannot change anything. The agent learns whether a job went out from the printer's state afterwards, not from the dialog.

# Fork stewardship
**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.
JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.
One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**
- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.
Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.
## The ten principles
### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much
**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.
**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.
**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?
**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.
### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge
**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.
**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.
**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?
**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.
### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it
**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.
**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.
**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?
**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.
### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism
**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.
**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.
**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?
**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.
### 5. One seam beats many touch points
**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

# After Send, nothing says the print went out: options

Working note, 2026-10-28, untracked. Branch checked: `jusprin-newui` at a684aee37d. Critique frames 1A-08 to 1A-12 in https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR.

## The problem

A person slices, presses Print, maps the "?" slot, presses Send in OrcaSlicer's Select Machine dialog and Confirm on its "unknown filaments" warning. The dialog closes and the window looks exactly as before: no line in the chat, nothing on the printer chip or header, the "1 print issue" pill unchanged. The job did go out.

## What I found

**Reproduction.** I launched a scratch copy of the 07:22 build with the fake A1 mini, but the request to control its window was declined, so I did not press Send myself and have no screenshot of my own. The evidence is the walkthrough session's log of the same build and the same steps, earlier today (`debug_Wed_Oct_28_05_47_26_46887.log.0`, lines 17006–17078 and after):

```
05:54:32.001  print_job: on_ok to send
05:54:32.176  FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=…/.46887.0.3mf
05:54:32.177  print_job: send ok.
05:54:32.189  skipped tab switch from 1 to 3, lack of network plugins
```

**Where the app learns the result.** On success `PrintJob::process` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/PrintJob.cpp:667`) queues `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED` carrying the device id. `Plater::print_job_finished` (`Plater.cpp:16575`) closes the dialog, selects that machine and asks for OrcaSlicer's **Device** tab. The Plater exposes the event id publicly (`Plater::get_print_finished_event()`, `get_send_finished_event()`), so fork code can bind it without touching OrcaSlicer. The fork binds neither today.

**Why the screen stays the same with the fake.** OrcaSlicer's own acknowledgement is that jump to the Device tab. `Plater::priv::on_tab_selection_changing` (`Plater.cpp:10303`) vetoes it when Bambu's network plug-in isn't loaded. The fake printer doesn't load it, and neither does Kenneth's own config (`installed_networking: false`). That veto is the "skipped tab switch" line above.

**What a real Bambu printer would probably do (from reading the code, not run).** Connecting a real Bambu printer requires the plug-in (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:340`). With the plug-in loaded the jump is not vetoed, and `ShellController::on_page_changed` shows the Notebook on its Device page, the same page as the printer menu's Monitor row. So on real hardware the person probably lands on OrcaSlicer's printer monitor after Send, not on an unchanged screen. **The fake hides this difference.** Whichever option is chosen, someone should check it once on a real printer.

**Failure.** On failure `PrintJob` writes OrcaSlicer's message into the dialog's own status bar (`ctl.show_error_info`, `PrintJob.cpp:658`, shown by `BBLStatusBarPrint`). It posts no event and no notification, and the dialog stays open. A failed send is therefore visible in the dialog but leaves nothing behind once the dialog is closed. The fake always succeeds, so testing failure needs a fork-owned switch in `Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp`, for example `"send_fails": true` in `fake_printer.json`.

**The ledger.** `SentRecord`, `add_sent` and `subscribe_ledger` exist, but no production code calls `add_sent` or `add_physical_print` (I grepped all of `src/`). The ledger has no record of this send. So the problem isn't a ledger with no reader; nothing is written at all.

**What the fork already has to build on:**
- `AgentHost::post_note(text, swatch)` adds a one-line note to the active chat, saves it with the project, starts no turn, and is not sent to the model. The header already uses it, through `StatusRow::set_note_sink`, for lines like a printer change. The page draws it as `.message note`.
- The issue pill's confirmations come only from OrcaSlicer's notification list (`NoticeKinds.cpp`, `JUSPRIN_RESULT_KINDS`). A successful print job posts no notification.
- The printer chip makes no claim about the machine. Idle / Printing / Offline appears only on the menu's first row (`PrinterMenu.cpp:84`), read from `MachineObject` when the menu opens.
- Print hosts (Klipper, OctoPrint) already get a chat entry: their upload is a `PrintHostUpload` notification, which `WorkFeed` turns into a work card. Only the Bambu path is silent.

## Options

### A. A one-line chat note when the dialog reports success (recommended)

- **What the person sees:** under the last message, within a second of the dialog closing, `Sent to Bambu Lab A1 mini 2 · 10:42`. It is drawn like the header's change lines, uses the chip's printer name, has no check mark, and stays in the chat and in the saved project. For Bambu's "Send to printer" (upload to storage only, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`) it says `Uploaded to … · not started`. A failure stays in the dialog as OrcaSlicer shows it today, and the chat gets no line.
- **OrcaSlicer lines:** none. A fork listener binds `get_print_finished_event()` and `get_send_finished_event()` on the Plater, calls `Skip()` so OrcaSlicer's handler still runs, and posts through the note sink the header already uses. Rebase cost: zero lines. The one dependency is that the two public getters keep existing; they haven't moved in a year.
- **Print history:** this is the history design's chat marker (`▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history`) without the hash and the link. The same listener is where the history work will write its G-code record and add those two parts. Nothing is thrown away, and notes written before then stay as plain lines.
- **Optional failure line:** a chat line such as `Not sent to … · <OrcaSlicer's reason>` needs OrcaSlicer to report a failure. That means one neutral seam in `PrintJob.cpp`'s failure branch: queue an event with the message, about 4 lines. That file had 23 upstream commits in the past year. I'd leave it out, because the dialog already stays open on the error.

### B. A short confirmation above the issue pill

- **What the person sees:** "Sent to Bambu Lab A1 mini 2" above the pill at the canvas's lower right, with a close button, the same way an export finishing is shown. It disappears when closed and is not in the chat or the saved project.
- **OrcaSlicer lines:** none. The listener from A would push the text through OrcaSlicer's public `NotificationManager::push_notification(text)`, which `NoticeKinds` already routes as a confirmation. But it puts JusPrin's words into the list that the architecture treats as OrcaSlicer's own ("OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth").
- **Print history:** no counterpart. The history design has no toast, so this would be removed or kept alongside the marker later. On real hardware the Device-tab jump also hides the canvas, so the confirmation would usually go unseen.

### C. The printer chip shows "Sending…", then the printer's state

- **What the person sees:** the chip reads Sending… from the press of Send until the job ends, then Printing once the printer reports it. On a LAN send the job takes about 10 ms, so Sending… barely shows. Printing arrives seconds later and only from the printer: the fake never reports it on its own.
- **OrcaSlicer lines:** nothing reports the moment Send is pressed. That needs a seam in `SelectMachineDialog::on_send_print`, in a file with 80 upstream commits in the past year. It also reverses the rule that the chip makes no claim about the machine, which is a design change for the chip in every state, not only after a send.
- **Print history:** the history design puts live progress on the printer card and on Print history's "Printing" row, not on the chip. Little of this would carry over.

### D. The agent speaks after the send (app-started turn)

- **What the person sees:** a few seconds later, an assistant message about the send. Nothing appears when no agent is set up, and nothing during a turn already running.
- **OrcaSlicer lines:** none. It would use the same listener as A, plus a new skill trigger, the same way `file_loaded` starts a turn today.
- **Against it:** every send costs a model call, the reply is slower than a note, and an acknowledgement that depends on the agent being configured is not an acknowledgement. Product definition §2.9: "The agent learns whether a job went out from the printer's state afterwards, not from the dialog." Under the history design the model reads sends from its state, so it doesn't need to be told.

## Recommendation

**A.** It is instant, it is in the place the person is already looking, it survives with the project, it touches no OrcaSlicer lines, and it is the first piece of the history marker rather than something the history work will remove. Failure stays in OrcaSlicer's dialog, which doesn't close on an error.

A decision that applies to every option: on a real Bambu printer, should OrcaSlicer's jump to its Device page after Send stay (it is OrcaSlicer's own acknowledgement and is reachable from the printer menu today), or should JusPrin keep the person on the project? If it stays, option A's note is what the person sees when they come back. This needs one check on real hardware before anyone relies on it.

## How A would be verified

Add a fork-only fake switch so that `start_local_print` can fail. Then, in the real app with the fake A1 mini: send successfully and screenshot the chat line; send with the switch on and screenshot the dialog's error, with no chat line; reopen the project and check the note is still there. Also add Catch2 coverage that the listener posts exactly one note per success event and none on failure, plus a Vitest check that the note renders.

I've written the options note, [sent-print-ack-options.md](sent-print-ack-options.md) (untracked, in the worktree root), and recommend option A: a one-line chat note after a successful send. I haven't changed any code, and I'm stopping here until Kenneth chooses.

**I didn't reproduce it myself.** I started a scratch copy of today's build with the fake A1 mini, but the request to control its window was declined. So I didn't press Send myself and have no screenshot of my own. The evidence is the log from the earlier walkthrough of the same steps on the same build: `print_job: send ok` at 05:54:32, followed immediately by `skipped tab switch from 1 to 3, lack of network plugins`.

**Why the screen stays the same:**
- **OrcaSlicer's own response to a successful send** is to close the dialog and switch to its Device tab (the printer monitor). It cancels that switch when Bambu's network plug-in isn't loaded. That's true for the fake printer and for Kenneth's own config.
- **With a real Bambu printer,** the plug-in has to be installed to connect, so the person would probably land on OrcaSlicer's Device page instead. I worked this out from the code and haven't run it. The fake printer hides this difference, so the critique's "nothing changes" may not match real hardware.
- **The print ledger records nothing.** No code in `src/` calls `add_sent`, so this isn't a ledger missing a reader.
- **A failed send** shows only in the dialog's own status line. The dialog stays open, and OrcaSlicer raises no event for it.

**The four options:**

| Option | What the person sees | OrcaSlicer lines changed | Fit with the print-history design |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A (recommended)** | `Sent to Bambu Lab A1 mini 2 · 10:42` in the chat, kept with the project | None | It's the history design's chat marker without the hash and link, so the history work builds on it |
| B | A short confirmation above the issue pill, gone once closed | None, but JusPrin's words go into the list treated as OrcaSlicer's | No counterpart in the history design; would be removed later |
| C | The printer chip shows "Sending…", then the printer's state | A change inside the send dialog, a busy upstream file | Reverses the rule that the chip makes no claim about the machine |
| D | The agent replies after the send | None | Costs a model call per send and shows nothing when no agent is set up |

For option A, the fork listens for OrcaSlicer's "print finished" event through a public getter on the Plater. It then posts the line through `AgentHost::post_note`, which the header already uses for its own one-line notes. A failure stays in the dialog. A failure line in the chat would need a seam of about 4 lines in `PrintJob.cpp`; I'd leave that out. One part is unconfirmed and should be tested first: that the fork's listener runs before OrcaSlicer's handler, since OrcaSlicer's handler doesn't pass the event on.

**One decision applies to every option:** on a real Bambu printer, should OrcaSlicer's jump to its Device page after Send stay, or should JusPrin keep the person on the project? Either way, it needs one check on real hardware.

I also left a short summary in the shared notes folder as `sent-print-ack.md`.

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth found 4 Release builds and 56 clang processes on 12 cores, all mine, in one worktree. Every ninja ran at its default -j (cores + 2), so 4 × 14 = 56. He pointed out that the orphaned processes were the smaller problem. The bigger one was that I put that many builds there at all.

What I did wrong, in order of weight:
1. I treated builds as free on a machine other sessions build on too. I never passed `-j`. I saw load 33, then 76, and started more builds anyway.
2. I restarted the build three times to change its target list or to slip in a small target. Each restart cost a full set of jobs. Waiting for the running build and adding targets afterwards cost nothing.
3. I went against the brief ("reuse the existing build; another session may be building") by configuring a fresh full-app build for an optional live check.
4. I blamed the slowness on "other sessions" without counting my own processes. That is the plausible-story-instead-of-checking failure from CLAUDE.md.
5. Mechanism: `pkill -f "cmake --build <dir>"` kills only the wrapper. Its `ninja -C <dir>` child keeps compiling as an orphan. I never checked that a stop had worked.

**Why:** the machine is shared. My extra jobs slow every other session, and two ninjas in one build dir can leave its records inconsistent.

**How to apply:**
- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. Cap jobs with `-- -j4` (fewer when load is above the core count).
- Decide the full target list once. Never restart a build to change it.
- Run one build per dir as its own process group (`set -m`, then kill with `kill -- -<pgid>`). After any stop, confirm with `pgrep -fl "ninja.*<dir>"`.
- Ask before a full-app build that the task did not require.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

old='### Application teardown can re-enter destroyed owners\n'
assert s.count(old)==1
new='''### A send's outcome is two Plater events, and only on success

OrcaSlicer's Bambu send dialogs run a job on their own worker. On success the
job queues one event on the Plater: `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED` from Select Machine
(`PrintJob`, the event's string is the device id) and `EVT_SEND_FINISHED` from
Send to Printer (`SendJob`, storage only; the string is the project name).
Neither event is declared in a header, but `Plater::get_print_finished_event()`
and `get_send_finished_event()` return their ids, so fork code binds them with
no OrcaSlicer line. OrcaSlicer's handlers close the dialog and do not skip; a
handler bound later runs first and must `Skip()` (`Shell/PrintMarkers`).

A failed job queues nothing and posts no notification: its words go to the
dialog's own status bar, and the dialog stays open.

`Plater::print_job_finished` also asks for OrcaSlicer's Device tab.
`on_tab_selection_changing` vetoes that switch while Bambu's network plug-in
is not loaded ("skipped tab switch … lack of network plugins"), which is the
case with the fake Bambu printer. A real Bambu printer needs the plug-in to
connect, so there the switch is expected to happen. That has not been checked
on hardware.

'''+old

content.text:
The sent-print marker is built and every automated test passes, but I couldn't finish the real-app check. It needs one approval from you for full-screen control. Everything is on branch `claude/peaceful-mayer-0dbd04` (based on jusprin-newui a684aee37d), uncommitted.

**What I built:**
- **Marker data and saving.** A chat note can carry print-marker data (kind, printer, plate number and plate name), and it is saved with the project. The page draws it as one line: "Sent to Bambu Lab A1 mini 2 · 12:53", with the plate in the tooltip. A storage-only send reads "Uploaded to … · not started".
- **Room for printer states later.** A future kind such as "printing" or "finished" only needs a new event source and one wording entry. A kind the page doesn't know yet still shows the host's plain text.
- **The listener.** It hears OrcaSlicer's two "send finished" events through the Plater's public getters, so no OrcaSlicer file changed. It lets OrcaSlicer's own handler run afterwards, so the dialog still closes.
  - The printer is named the way the header names it.
  - For a storage-only upload it names the machine OrcaSlicer has selected, because that event carries the project name instead of a printer.
- **Failures.** A failed send stays in OrcaSlicer's dialog and adds no chat line.
- **Test switch.** The fake printer now accepts `"send_fails": true` in its control file, which makes the next send fail.
- **Docs.** I added a section to `orca-integration-guide.md` and one line to `architecture.md`.

**What I verified:**
- **Handler order:** I confirmed in the wxWidgets source that a handler bound later runs first.
- **Catch2:** all three suites pass in full: agent_bridge_tests (448 cases), shell_theme_tests (14) and jusprin_fake_bambu_tests (11). That includes the new ones: one note per successful send, none for a different event or after the shell is gone, the marker saved with the project, an unknown kind refused, and the fake failing on request.
- **Tests can fail:** the listener test fails if the hand-off to OrcaSlicer's handler is removed, and the Vitest marker test fails if the line's rendering is removed.
- **Vitest:** 616 tests in 31 files pass, and the TypeScript type check is clean.

**What isn't verified:** the real-app run. In a scratch copy of the new build with the fake A1 mini, I removed the file's two extra objects, sliced, and opened the send dialog. It is still open on "JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)" with Send not yet pressed. Pressing a button in OrcaSlicer's dialogs needs full-screen control, and that request timed out with no answer. So these two screenshots are missing:
- the chat line after a successful send;
- the dialog's error after a send with `send_fails` on, with no chat line.

The plan was also to reopen the project afterwards and check the line is still there. A new build-only finding: the app's automatic reply when the file opened is a live model call, so this run made one.

   - `Plater::print_job_finished` closes the dialog and requests the tpMonitor (Device) tab. `Plater::priv::on_tab_selection_changing` vetoes that tab when `!NetworkAgent::is_network_module_loaded()`, which is the fake-printer case.
   - wx dynamic handlers run in reverse binding order. Confirmed in wx `event.cpp`: `DoBind` does `push_back`, and `SearchDynamicEventTable` iterates from the end. So the fork handler runs before OrcaSlicer's and must `Skip()`.

content.text:
I've built the sent-print chat note on branch `claude/peaceful-mayer-0dbd04`, but I couldn't check it in the real app. After a successful send from OrcaSlicer's send dialog, a one-line note like "Sent to JusPrin Fake A1 mini · 13:05" appears in the chat and is saved with the project. Nothing is committed, and no OrcaSlicer-owned file was changed.

**How it works:**
- A new listener, `PrintMarkers` in `Shell/PrintMarkers.cpp`, hooks the two public "finished" events OrcaSlicer fires on the Plater (the main slicer view):
  - **print-finished** means the job was sent and started. It becomes "Sent to …".
  - **send-finished** means the file was only stored on the printer. It becomes "Uploaded to … · not started".
- The listener passes each event on to OrcaSlicer's own handler, which still closes the dialog as before.
- A failed send fires neither event, so the error stays in OrcaSlicer's dialog and nothing goes in the chat.
- The note is a new kind of saved chat note that carries:
  - the printer name,
  - the event kind (sent or uploaded),
  - the time,
  - the plate number and name.

  Printer states such as Printing, Paused or Finished can later reuse the same line as new event sources.
- The fake Bambu printer has a new test switch, `"send_fails": true` in `fake_printer.json`, which makes its send fail.

**Verified:**
- **Handler order:** wxWidgets runs the handler bound last first, which I confirmed in its `event.cpp`. So my handler runs before OrcaSlicer's and passes the event on.
- **Build:** the Release build of the app and the test targets succeeds.
- **C++ tests:** agent bridge 448 cases, shell 14, fake Bambu printer 11, all passing.
- **Web tests:** Vitest 616 pass and the TypeScript check is clean.
- **The tests catch breakage:** removing the pass-on call fails the C++ ordering test, and removing the chat-line rendering fails the Vitest marker test.

**Not verified: the real-app send with the fake A1 mini.** The send dialog opened ready to go with Send enabled, but in about ten tries neither clicks nor key presses reached the button. The log never shows `print_job: on_ok to send`. I saw three likely causes:
- A mouse button was left held down after an earlier release attempt was refused. Windows dragged along with the cursor until I released it.
- The modal dialog ended up hidden behind the main window.
- The screen-control tool reported every point of the dialog as belonging to "a different process".

I've closed the scratch app. These screenshots are missing:
1. The chat line after a successful send.
2. A failed send (`send_fails` on), showing the error in the dialog and no chat line.
3. The note still there after reopening the project.

Status and these details are also in the shared notes file `sent-print-ack.md`.

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before

I still can't get a confirmed send, because none of my clicks or key presses reach OrcaSlicer's "Send print job" dialog. Which monitor the app was on was not the cause. The app is ready for you to press Send yourself, and I'll check the result as soon as you have.

**Where the app is:**
- I checked both monitors by window position. Every JusPrin window is on the laptop screen, which is the main display (1728×1117 points). The external monitor, which now reports as "SB220Q", sits above it at negative coordinates.
- The send dialog is the topmost window at the Send button; nothing covers it.
- The project is open and sliced, and the dialog shows "JusPrin Fake A1 mini(LAN)" ready to send.

**Why my input doesn't reach the dialog:**
- I captured the app's main-thread stack while the dialog was open. OrcaSlicer opens it from a queued event (`Plater::priv::on_action_print_plate`, then `ShowModal`) while wx is running a run-loop callback. Its modal loop then waits for events inside that callback.
- In that state, none of my synthetic mouse clicks or key presses changed the dialog. Clicking Send, toggling Timelapse and pressing Return all did nothing.
- The background click tool refuses the dialog outright: it reports every point as "a different process".
- Normal, non-modal screens work. Clicking a project card on the Home page opened the project, and Cmd+R sliced it.
- So I can't press Send myself. Whether real hardware clicks get through is untested; that is what pressing Send yourself will show.

**Problems I hit on the way:**
- **Wrong launch method:** I had started the app binary directly from my shell. That copy drew its windows but took no input. Launching it with `open -n` fixed that.
- **Permission prompt on startup:** the app's recent-files list pointed into ~/Downloads, which macOS protects. Reading the thumbnails raised a permission prompt that froze startup. I trimmed the list in the scratch app's own settings file rather than answer the prompt, which is your call to make.
- **A separate JusPrin bug:** starting the app with a project file shows the "Previously opened file" prompt during startup. In that state the prompt accepts no input of any kind, so the app sits there for good. I hit this twice. It comes from fork code in `ShellController::install`, called during `post_init`. I have not fixed it, and it should get its own task.

**What happens after you press Send:**
1. I check the log for the send and screenshot the chat line, which should read "Sent to JusPrin Fake A1 mini · HH:MM".
2. I switch the fake printer to `send_fails` and send again, ideally with you pressing Send again. I screenshot the error in the dialog and confirm no chat line appears.
3. I reopen the project to confirm the line was saved with it.

Nothing is committed. The code is unchanged since the last report, and the unit tests and Vitest still pass.

Show a one-line chat note when a print goes out

After Send in OrcaSlicer's send dialog, nothing in JusPrin said the job had

sent and started, or "Uploaded to <printer> · not started" when it was only
stored on the printer. The note is saved with the project.

PrintMarkers binds the Plater's public print-finished and send-finished
events (no OrcaSlicer lines change). wx runs the handler bound last first,
so it runs before OrcaSlicer's own handler and skips on to it. A failed send
queues neither event, so its error stays in OrcaSlicer's dialog and the chat
says nothing.

The note carries a printer event (kind, printer, plate) so later printer
states such as Printing or Finished can reuse the same line as new event
sources. The fake Bambu printer gains a send_fails switch for testing the
failure path.

One record per G-code that left a project replaces the Sent events and

20:**Where the app learns the result.** On success `PrintJob::process` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/PrintJob.cpp:667`) queues `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED` carrying the device id. `Plater::print_job_finished` (`Plater.cpp:16575`) closes the dialog, selects that machine and asks for OrcaSlicer's **Device** tab. The Plater exposes the event id publicly (`Plater::get_print_finished_event()`, `get_send_finished_event()`), so fork code can bind it without touching OrcaSlicer. The fork binds neither today.
22:**Why the screen stays the same with the fake.** OrcaSlicer's own acknowledgement is that jump to the Device tab. `Plater::priv::on_tab_selection_changing` (`Plater.cpp:10303`) vetoes it when Bambu's network plug-in isn't loaded. The fake printer doesn't load it, and neither does Kenneth's own config (`installed_networking: false`). That veto is the "skipped tab switch" line above.
31:- `AgentHost::post_note(text, swatch)` adds a one-line note to the active chat, saves it with the project, starts no turn, and is not sent to the model. The header already uses it, through `StatusRow::set_note_sink`, for lines like a printer change. The page draws it as `.message note`.
41:- **OrcaSlicer lines:** none. A fork listener binds `get_print_finished_event()` and `get_send_finished_event()` on the Plater, calls `Skip()` so OrcaSlicer's handler still runs, and posts through the note sink the header already uses. This depends on wxWidgets calling the handler bound later first; OrcaSlicer's handler doesn't call `Skip()`. That ordering is unverified here and is the first thing to test. Rebase cost: zero lines. The one dependency is that the two public getters keep existing; they haven't moved in a year.
49:- **Print history:** no counterpart. The history design has no toast, so this would be removed or kept alongside the marker later. On real hardware the Device-tab jump also hides the canvas, so the confirmation would usually go unseen.
53:- **What the person sees:** the chip reads Sending… from the press of Send until the job ends, then Printing once the printer reports it. On a LAN send the job takes about 10 ms, so Sending… barely shows. Printing arrives seconds later and only from the printer: the fake never reports it on its own.
59:- **What the person sees:** a few seconds later, an assistant message about the send. Nothing appears when no agent is set up, and nothing during a turn already running.
71:Add a fork-only fake switch so that `start_local_print` can fail. Then, in the real app with the fake A1 mini: send successfully and screenshot the chat line; send with the switch on and screenshot the dialog's error, with no chat line; reopen the project and check the note is still there. Also add Catch2 coverage that the listener posts exactly one note per success event and none on failure, plus a Vitest check that the note renders.

content.text:
The decision that reached me settled what happens on a send and deliberately left printer events like a failed print for later. It said nothing about what happens when there's no active chat. If you discussed that in the parent session, "Common Jusprin user flows", it didn't reach me.

**What was decided.** The parent session relayed this from you after you said "go with this approach":
- **Option A:** after a send, one dated line appears in the chat, such as "Sent to Bambu Lab A1 mini 2 · 10:42". If the file was only stored on the printer, it reads "Uploaded to … · not started".
- **One reusable marker type.** It is for events that happen outside the project. It records the printer name, the kind of event, the time and the plate.
- **In scope now:** only the sent and uploaded cases.
- **Later, not wired now:** the printer's own state changes, "Printing", "Paused", "Failed" and "Finished". The marker was built so these can be added later as new event sources without a new kind of line.
- **A failed send:** OrcaSlicer's dialog shows the error and the chat says nothing. This is the send itself failing, not a print failing later on the printer.
- **Other rules:** the note is saved with the project, and no OrcaSlicer files change.

**What wasn't decided:**
1. **Failed prints and other printer events** arrive later, after the send. They were explicitly deferred. Nothing in my commit listens to the printer after the send.
2. **No active chat.** This wasn't part of the decision. From reading the code, without testing it: my note goes to the project's *active* chat. If the project has no active chat, the save step silently does nothing, yet the page is still told about the new line. So the line could appear and then vanish when the project is reopened. I also don't know whether a project can be open with no active chat in practice. Separately, if you're viewing a different chat than the active one, the line goes to the active one, not the one in front of you.

**The print-history commit.** Your commit on origin today, ebbb2f8894, already adds a chat marker where a G-code leaves the project. It also tracks printer reports after a send: it polls Bambu printers and records started and finished prints. So it covers part of point 1, which my commit never did. I haven't checked how it handles no active chat.

That's why I still think dropping my commit is the right call. The open question, if you want it settled, is how print history's marker behaves with no active chat. That's a check against its code, not mine.
Drop mine
